entry.title: SAP ME/MII msg type yieldConfirmationRequest goes into RETRY status and MESYS blocks reservation
entry.content:
Hi Experts ,

 

Did you faced these behaviours:

     SAP ME/MII native message type yieldConfirmationRequest goes always into RETRY status when is processed for the

first time and only when the message is re-processed , the second time , it goes into correct status PASSED ; This is not good

at all because it increasing the processing time of the messages inside the MII queue ;

     The second behavior is that the componentAddRequest message always goes first into FAILED status with the message:

User MESYS blocks the reservation xxxxxxxxxxxx  ; Those kind of failed messages became PASSED only if they are manually RETRY; This is not good also because a time consuming manually intervention is needed  ;

    The above behaviours appeared after we installed: 

                                    SAP ME 15.5 Patch 43 first and then Patch 44 , SAP XMII 15.5.2.1 and  SAP MII_ADMIN 15.5.2.1 ;

    Thank you in advance for your help !

 

Best Regards,

Paul

Our client has 5 SPC Lines. When we create production order for these SPC Lines, the order is assigned to the workcenter as SPC1 (Operation 0020) and SPCW1(Operation 0010) for SPC Line 1. We can see the order in MES system for SPC Line 1 which is a custom screen designed using MII BLS and UI5. When the IDOC is released to MES, it get's processed by a Workflow configured in MII (XSLT file) and the data is stored in MES. 

When we create orders for SPC5 line and released into MES, the order is not visible in MES SPC Line 5 screen. The order has been processed successfully, also available in Shop order maintenance. I also checked in the ROUTER_OPERATION Table in MII, both the 0010 and 0020 operations are available for the order. 

Is there a way to understand why we are not able to see the SPC5 order in the MES screen?

entry.title: PCo OPC UA: How to ensure consistent multi-tag data when a trigger fires?
entry.content:
We are investigating an intermittent data consistency issue with SAP PCo and an OPC UA source and would appreciate input on the recommended implementation pattern.

A machine PLC exposes multiple process/result values plus a Boolean trigger through its integrated OPC UA server.

The sequence in the PLC is essentially:

  1. Write all process/result values

  2. Set ResultComplete = TRUE

PCo subscribes to these tags. When ResultComplete becomes TRUE, a PCo notification is triggered and the subscribed result values are passed to an SAP MII transaction.

Intermittently, the trigger is received correctly, but some of the associated result values are still empty or contain their previous value.

We have observed the same behavior on equipment from different suppliers. Adding a short delay between writing the process values and setting the trigger resolves the issue, but we consider this a timing workaround rather than a robust synchronization mechanism.

Our current assumption is that the PLC application cycle and the OPC UA server sampling/update cycle are not synchronized. The OPC UA server may therefore expose the new trigger before all other OPC UA nodes belonging to the same logical dataset have been refreshed.

How should PCo reliably obtain the current dataset once the trigger has been detected? In particular:

  • Is there a recommended PCo pattern for trigger detected → fresh read of required OPC UA tags → process data → acknowledge PLC?

  • Would a PCo Retrieve Query after detecting the trigger perform a fresh OPC UA Read, or could it still return values currently held by the OPC UA server?

  • If PCo performs an OPC UA Read, is the OPC UA maxAge configurable or known? Can PCo request a fresh value from the underlying data source (maxAge = 0)?

  • Is there another PCo mechanism intended to ensure consistency of a logical dataset consisting of multiple independently exposed OPC UA nodes?

  • What is the recommended approach to avoid relying on an arbitrary PLC-side delay?

We would prefer to keep the process values as individual OPC UA tags, as a single MES transaction can contain many values and combining them into one tag/structure solely for synchronization would add considerable complexity.

Any experience with this scenario, particularly with PCo OPC UA notifications and Retrieve Queries, would be very helpful.

entry.title: Request for SAP ME 15.5 Full Course and Preconfigured Practice System help
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community Members,

I am an MES Support Engineer working in electronics manufacturing, with around 8 years of experience in MES support.

I am planning to learn SAP Manufacturing Execution (SAP ME 15.5) end to end, including configuration, production execution, and ERP integration.

I have already collected SAP ME documentation covering application help, master data, shop-floor execution, reporting, and SAPMEINT integration. However, I am looking for a structured learning path and, most importantly, a preconfigured SAP ME 15.5 practice system where I can perform hands-on exercises.

I would like to practice the following:

Site, Material, Resource, Operation, and Routing configuration

Shop Order creation and SFC management

POD configuration and production execution

Component consumption and genealogy tracking

Data Collection, Nonconformance, and Rework

Reporting and troubleshooting

SAP ERP integration using SAPMEINT

Could anyone please guide me on the following?

Is there an official SAP ME 15.5 course or complete learning path available for individual learners?

Is any preconfigured SAP ME 15.5 training or practice server available?

Can an individual learner obtain temporary access to a sandbox or training tenant?

If SAP ME 15.5 practice access is no longer available, what is the best way to obtain hands-on access to SAP Digital Manufacturing (SAP DM)?

I am looking for actual system access to practice configurations and production scenarios, rather than theory-only training or documentation.

If anyone has experience with SAP ME training environments or can recommend a legitimate access option, I would greatly appreciate your guidance.

Thank you for your time and support!
